Subject: Initial DPA request and e-sign preference

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo last week — Pelago is excited to move forward. Legal asked me to collect our standard privacy paperwork before we proceed with provisioning. Could you please: 

- Share Redwood's current DPA template (preferably PDF and Word).
- Confirm whether you accept DocuSign or AdobeSign for execution.
- Provide an up-to-date subprocessors list and a short note on any EU data transfers (SCCs or equivalent).

We can start a quick review internally once we have the materials. Our SLA & data residency requirements are modest but we do need clarity on subprocessor categories (analytics, hosting, monitoring).

If you'd prefer, feel free to loop in your privacy lead — happy to sync on a short call as well.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Lemaire
Head of Legal Ops, Pelago

- We attach our current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) and Word version.
- We support DocuSign and AdobeSign; DocuSign preferred for template flows.
- We will provide the current subprocessor list (subprocessor_list_2027-03.csv) and confirm SCC usage for EU transfers.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial DPA request and e-sign preference (Pelago)

Thanks for the ping — reviewed Pelago_Redlines.docx. High level: Pelago's redlines are largely standard requests but they added an unusual clause asking for a contractually guaranteed egress window for historical logs (48 hours). We should push back — acceptable to offer an operational commitment (we'll provide an export within X days upon request) but not a contractual SLA for log exports at this time.

Specifics to update in response: 
- Approve sending Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf and the Word copy.
- Attach subprocessor_list_2027-03.csv and the SCCs packet (Redwood_SCCs.pdf).
- For signatures, state we 'support DocuSign and AdobeSign; DocuSign preferred. Execution via either is legally binding.'
- For subprocessor notice, change Pelago's suggested 30 days to our standard 21 days.
- Push on log egress SLA; offer to include an operational note in the SOW and route technical details to CS.

I'll redact our internal risk assessment notes from the document and create a small reply template. Rafael, once you get their confirmation on e-sign, send the DocuSign powerform link and attach the files.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Hi Sophie — thanks, and great to hear Pelago is moving forward. Attaching the items Marissa approved: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf (PDF and Word), current subprocessor_list_2027-03.csv, and our SCCs packet (Redwood_SCCs.pdf). Also attached is a short note that clarifies our standard subprocessor-notice window (21 days) and how we handle transfers out of the EU.

To confirm execution options: we accept both DocuSign and AdobeSign. For efficiency we typically send a DocuSign PowerForm for the DPA (link below). If Pelago prefers AdobeSign, we can route there instead — just let me know.

DocuSign PowerForm (DPA): https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-1234
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/421/PEL-4872

A couple of clarifying points we included in the cover note: 
- Subprocessors are grouped by function (hosting, monitoring, analytics). We will notify Pelago of new subprocessors at least 21 days prior to onboarding.
- For EU transfers, Redwood relies on standard SCCs between the controller/processor where applicable and we provide copies upon request (attached).
- Regarding export/egress of logs: we can provide an operational export within 5 business days for standard requests; for high-volume historical exports we will scope effort in the SOW.

Please confirm which e-sign tool you'd like (DocuSign or AdobeSign) and whether Pelago prefers a counter-signed PDF returned to contracts@pelago.com or a direct DocuSign completion. Once you confirm, I'll send the PowerForm.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
